title: TTL: Support TTL over Ethernet
description:
The external taps use an unregistered Ethertype to send the data to the main logger, that writes everything to file.

The format of the TTL entry is exactly the same. This MR splits the common code from file-ttl to packet-ttl, and adds the appropriate Ethertype.

While we're at it, dissect encapsulated Ethernet, CAN, LIN and FlexRay. Some changes to the respective dissectors were needed.

Cab you look this warning 

`Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-ttl.c hf_ttl_trace_data_entry_status_info_can_flags filter= ttl.trace_data.entry.status_info.can_flags  - mask with non-contiguous bits 0xf00f ( 0xf00f )Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-ttl.c hf_ttl_trace_data_entry_status_info_fr_error_flags filter= ttl.trace_data.entry.status_info.fr_flags  - mask with non-contiguous bits 0x07e8 ( 0x7e8 )Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-ttl.c hf_ttl_trace_data_entry_status_info_fr_pulse_flags filter= ttl.trace_data.entry.status_info.fr_pulse_flags  - mask with non-contiguous bits 0xe808 ( 0xe808 )`

These were already there, and that's because the flags are really non-contiguous according to the TTL specification.
Is is better to split them into multiple flag fields?
No, they may be ignored, or (better) I can mark them as exception in the checking script
Should be fixed in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22120 (merged)
can you share also some file ? (do you have fuzz the code ?)
Unfortunately I can't share any capture because it includes sensitive data.
